Dengue Encephalitis: The patient presents with fever, vomiting, weakness in all four limbs, speech difficulty, and bilateral horizontal gaze palsy, which are consistent with neurological involvement in dengue fever. The presence of positive serum dengue NS1 antigen and the MRI findings of bilateral thalamic lesions support this diagnosis.
Acute Flaccid Myelitis: The patient's symptoms of acute weakness in all four limbs and bilateral extensor plantar responses could also be consistent with acute flaccid myelitis, although the presence of bilateral thalamic lesions on MRI and positive dengue NS1 antigen make dengue encephalitis a more likely diagnosis.
